cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles by the Kebar River, is the one telling us this (Ezekiel 1:1-3). In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month, some of the elders of Israel come to inquire of the LORD, and they sit down in front of him. Then the word of the LORD comes to the prophet.

cards.question: The elders of Israel came to Ezekiel to inquire of the LORD. What is the Lord GOD's answer to them?

answers.text: He will not be consulted by them
He will answer the oldest one

cards.text: They came to ask the LORD something, and the answer is NO, as surely as He lives. That's sitting through forty minutes of hold music just to hear, "Our office is closed."

Instead, God tells Ezekiel to confront them with the abominations of their fathers, all the way back in Egypt. On the day He chose Israel, He made Himself known to them there and said, "I am the LORD your God."

cards.question: God swore to bring Israel out of Egypt into a land flowing with milk and honey. True or false: God says He searched out that land for them Himself.
While they're still in Egypt, God tells each of them to throw away the abominations before his eyes. What else must they not defile themselves with?
Israel has God's command. True or false: a few of them cast away the abominations before their eyes.

cards.text: Not one of them. They rebel and refuse to listen. That's asking the group chat for ONE volunteer and getting left on read by EVERYBODY.

cards.question: God resolved to pour out His wrath on Israel right there in the land of Egypt. But He holds back. Why?

answers.text: For the sake of His name

cards.question: God acts for the sake of His name, so it won't be profaned in someone's eyes. Whose eyes?

cards.text: So God brings them out of Egypt and leads them into the wilderness. ONE verse! It took me years and an angel to get out of a junk drawer.

cards.question: In the wilderness, God gives them His statutes and ordinances. He says the man who does these things will ___ by them.
God also gives Israel His Sabbaths as a sign between Him and them. True or false: the sign is so they'll know He is the LORD who sanctifies them.

cards.text: Round two, in the wilderness: Israel rejects His ordinances and utterly profanes His Sabbaths, so God resolves to put an end to them there. And AGAIN, He acts for the sake of His name.

cards.question: Then, in the wilderness, God swears an oath to that generation with an uplifted hand. What does He swear?

answers.text: He won't bring them into the land
He'll send them back to Egypt
He'll give them a new king

cards.question: God gives the reason for His oath: they kept rejecting His ordinances and profaning His Sabbaths, for their hearts continually went after their ___.
After all that rebellion, true or false: God destroys that generation and brings them to an end in the wilderness.

cards.text: Instead, God looks on them with pity and does not destroy them. Friend, I have seen LESS patience than that at a four-way stop.
Now God turns to their children, out in the wilderness. He tells them not to walk in the statutes of their fathers or defile themselves with their fathers' idols.

cards.question: God tells the children not to walk in their fathers' statutes. Whose statutes does He tell them to walk in instead?
God tells the children to keep His ___ holy, as a sign between Him and them.
The children get a fresh start in the wilderness. True or false: they walk in God's statutes and carefully keep His ordinances.

cards.text: Nope. The children rebel and profane His Sabbaths too. That's the brand-new planner you buy in January that's blank by February.
God resolves to pour out His wrath on them in the wilderness. But once again, He withholds His hand for the sake of His name.

cards.question: Even so, God swears an oath to the children in the wilderness with an uplifted hand. What does He swear?

answers.text: He'll scatter them among the nations
He'll make them a great empire
He'll send them back to Egypt

cards.question: What reason does God give for scattering the children among the nations?

answers.text: They fixed their eyes on their fathers' idols
They married wives from the nations
They asked Samuel to give them a king

cards.text: Then comes a hard part. God says He gave them over to statutes that were not good, and pronounced them unclean through their gifts: the sacrifice of every firstborn in the fire.

cards.question: God says He did this so that He might devastate them. True or false: He says it's in order that they would know that He is the LORD.

cards.text: Then God tells Ezekiel to speak to the house of Israel: this is another way their fathers blasphemed Him. Once God brought them into the land He swore to give them, they started offering sacrifices, incense and drink offerings.

cards.question: In the land, the fathers offer their sacrifices wherever they see any high ___ or leafy ___.
God asks them, "What is this high place to which you go?" What is that place called, to this day?

cards.text: Bamah. God asks about that high place, and the name sticks to this day. That's the nickname from your first week at work that is SOMEHOW still on the break room whiteboard.
Now God brings it right up to the people of Ezekiel's day. He asks the house of Israel if they'll defile themselves the way their fathers did.

cards.question: True or false: God says the house of Israel in Ezekiel's day is still sacrificing their sons in the fire and defiling themselves with idols.

cards.text: So God gives the same answer He gave at the start: as surely as He lives, He will not be consulted by them. They came in with ONE question and got the whole family history.
Then God takes on something the house of Israel says. They've got a plan for who they want to be.

cards.question: The house of Israel says, Let us be like someone, serving wood and stone. Like who?
They want to be like the nations, serving wood and stone. True or false: God says what they have in mind will come to pass.

cards.text: As surely as He lives, God says He will rule over them with a strong hand, an outstretched arm and outpoured wrath. They want to blend in with the nations, and God says He's still the One in charge.

cards.question: With that same strong hand, God will bring them out from the peoples and ___ them from the lands where they've been scattered.

cards.text: But first, God brings them into the wilderness of the nations. No shortcuts, friend.

cards.question: What will God do with His people there in the wilderness of the nations?

answers.text: Enter into judgment face to face
Teach them to build an ark

cards.text: It's just like He judged their fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt. He'll make them pass under the rod and bring them into the bond of the covenant.

cards.question: God will purge out the ones who rebel and transgress against Him. True or false: those rebels will still enter the land of Israel.

cards.text: Then God says something you might not see coming. He tells the house of Israel, Go and serve your idols, every one of you.

cards.question: God tells the house of Israel to go serve their idols. But what does He say will happen afterward?

answers.text: They will surely listen to Him
They will forget Him for good
They will never go home again

cards.text: Afterward, they'll surely listen, and they'll stop defiling His holy name. Me? I tell customers to go try the bakery down the street, knowing FULL well mine's the only bakery on this planet.

cards.question: God says the whole house of Israel, all of them, will serve Him in the land. Where?
Earlier, God refused to be consulted by them. True or false: on His holy mountain, God says He will accept them and their offerings.
When God gathers them from the lands where they were scattered, He says He will accept them as a pleasing ___.

cards.text: A pleasing aroma! Friend, I run a BAKERY, I know that one: the oven door opens on a fresh batch and suddenly EVERYBODY has a reason to walk past.
God will show His holiness through them in the sight of the nations. Then they will know He is the LORD, when He brings them into the land He swore to give their fathers.

cards.question: Back in the land, they'll remember their ways and all the deeds that defiled them. How does God say they'll feel about themselves?

answers.text: They will be proud of themselves

cards.question: They will know He is the LORD when He deals with them for the sake of His name, and not according to their ___ ways.

cards.text: After round after round of rebellion, God deals with them for the sake of His name, not their record. And as a stamper who got pulled out of the back of a junk drawer, friend, I know a little something about that.
